entities.summary:
Mikhail Vsevolodovich, known as Michael or Michael of Chernigov, was Grand Prince of Kiev ; he was also Prince of Pereyaslavl (1206), Novgorod-Seversk (1219–1226), Chernigov, Novgorod, and Galicia (1235–1236).

Born around 1157, he ascended to the throne of Kiev after the death of his father, Vsevolod III, in 1216. His reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against neighboring tribes and the Mongol invasion of Eastern Europe. Michael implemented various administrative reforms, including the establishment of a new system of governance for the vast territories under his control.

He was canonized as a saint in the Christian Church, and his legacy continued to shape the political landscape of Eastern Europe for centuries to come.

The Michael of Chernigov's diplomatic efforts with the Mongols and his strategic alliances with other princes led to a brief period of peace, known as the 'Golden Age' of Chernigov, which saw significant economic growth and cultural flourishing.

Today, the city of Chernigov, now known as Chernihiv, remains a testament to Michael's enduring legacy, with its well-preserved medieval architecture and rich history.

The Michael of Chernigov's commitment to the Christian faith and his role as a unifying force for the Orthodox Church have made him a revered figure in Eastern European history.
